      "observations": [
        "The owned patch restores the previous focus target after Send, Ignore and the notification close button. It captures parent.document.activeElement before adding the bar, updates a local lastActiveElement from focusin.relatedTarget, and uses the parent target only when that local target is absent. The commit title does not describe an unconditional thread-pane focus operation.",
        "The exact accepted setMDNMsg retains this implementation. HandleMDNResponse only installs the bar when the MDN generator asks the user; SendMDNResponse and IgnoreMDNResponse forward userAgreed and userDeclined.",
        "Each setMDNMsg call registers a document focusin closure without once, signal or a local removal. The inspected clearMsgNotifications removes notification elements. This is a bounded static lifetime observation; it does not establish a reproduced leak, focus failure or effect of an engine implementation.",
        "No test file changes in this patch. The accepted return-receipt test recreates several receipt-header/address combinations and checks notification presence and text; it has no focused-element assertion. Its custom errors and final Assert.report carry nonempty expected-state messages. The final completion message lacks should, which alone is not a patch defect.",
        "The callback names and focus helper make the target relationship explicit. Source inspection does not establish a visible focus ring or screen-reader outcome.",
        "Complete primary Bug 1976645 retains the reporter's focus/scroll symptom and historical version reports. A larger upstream notification implementation was suggested, but its body is outside this comm audit.",
        "Complete D284817 rejects a generic thread-pane focus action and asks to capture and restore the previous target. The landed and fixed accepted source implements that choice. The author reports correct focus with an absent ring in one header-button case and arrow-key confirmation; these are historical reports, not fresh keyboard or accessibility results."
